facts.fact: The Sfax Court of Appeal sentenced journalist Haythem El Mekki to one year in prison on 15 July 2026, requalifying the case from Decree-Law 54 to Article 86 of the Telecommunications Code, over a social-media post on the situation at a Sfax hospital (complaint by the hospital); a first-instance court had dismissed it.
Lawyer and commentator Sonia Dahmani was arrested in May 2024 and later convicted several times for remarks made on broadcast programmes, per Nawaat.

Journalists Borhen Bsaies and Mourad Zeghidi were sentenced to one year in prison, reduced to eight months, for statements under Decree-Law 54; the document gives no date for the sentence, so the document's publication date 2026-07-16 is used.

Abir Moussi, president of the Free Destourian Party, was sentenced to two years in prison for spreading false news about the electoral authority; the document gives no date for the sentence, so the document's publication date 2026-07-16 is used.

The National Union of Tunisian Journalists (SNJT), with Human Rights Watch, Amnesty International and RSF, denounced Decree-Law 2022-54 as a tool of repression, and the SNJT called for the annulment of the El Mekki judgment; the SNJT is inside the country; the criticism is reported in the document dated 2026-07-16.
RSF reports that on 15 July 2026 journalist and columnist Haythem El Mekki was sentenced to one year in prison over a post denouncing conditions in a hospital morgue.
RSF says that in 2024 over ten journalists in Tunisia were targeted by legal proceedings for doing their jobs, among them Mourad Zeghidi, held since 11 May 2024.
RSF says the radio station Diwan FM keeps a balanced, critical approach to the political news cycle; no named policy is given and no date, so the document's publication date 2026-04-30 is used.

RSF says the National Union of Tunisian Journalists (SNJT) protested the presidential palace no longer receiving journalists since 2019; no date for the protest is given, so the publication date 2026-04-30 is used.

note: Convictions of Zied El Heni and Khaoula Boukrim are named only in a headline, and Zeghidi's detention gives no statement: no fact.
Cloud-hosting circular for public bodies; says nothing on cuts, speech or criticism.

facts.fact: Lawyer and columnist Sonia Dahmani was sentenced to two years in May 2026 for criticising prison conditions in a radio interview, charged under Decree 54, per Al Jazeera.
The journalists' union SNJT and civil society groups demanded Decree 54 be scrapped altogether, per Al Jazeera.

CPJ reports lawyer and commentator Sonia Dahmani was convicted on 25 May 2026 under Decree-Law 54 of spreading false news likely to harm a public official over 2023 comments criticising prison conditions, and sentenced to two years, free pending appeal.
CPJ says journalist Ghassen Ben Khelifa was sentenced to two years in prison in March 2026.

Access Now, citing OONI anomaly data, says widespread mobile internet disruptions affecting messaging apps hit Tunisia during the Baccalaureate session from 3 June 2026 and again 29 June to 2 July 2026.
CPJ says the Sfax Court of Appeal sentenced commentator Haythem el-Mekki on 8 July 2026 to one year over a social media post denouncing failings at a hospital.
CPJ says Sonia Dahmani received an 18-month sentence on appeal in April 2026 over remarks on migrants and another two-year sentence in May 2026 over remarks on prison conditions.
CPJ says journalists Zied el-Heni, Mourad Zghidi and Borhen Bsaies are currently behind bars in Tunisia.

The Times of Tunis reports that authorities jammed signals around baccalaureate exam venues from 4 June 2026, disrupting WhatsApp and Messenger in several regions, while officials said no nationwide internet cut was decided.
The journalists' union SNJT, on 11 April 2025, called on MPs to annul the 'liberticide' articles of decree-law 54 and in February 2025 adopted a motion demanding its cancellation.

SNJT president Zied Dabbar says journalists, lawyers, bloggers and citizens are being prosecuted under decree-law 54, and the report notes lawyer and columnist Sonia Dahmani is accused under its Article 24.

note: Cassation ruling of 3 February 2025 limits decree-law 54 away from audiovisual media; it is not a repeal or strike-down of an offence.
Only the slowness of digitalisation is criticised, not a named government policy; no cut or punishment stated.
Closure of an oversight body and a press freedom rank are not a cut or punishment for speech.
